hits.title: Consumer support outcome: good practices and areas for improvement | FCA
hits.snippet:
Smaller firms

Where smaller firms cannot access similar tools, they may consider proportionate methods to monitor whether customers are receiving the support they need. This could include periodic call listening or file reviews using a simple checklist, for example, checking whether customer needs were identified, appropriate support was provided, and issues were resolved without repeat contact. [...] Firms that monitor a range of customer support metrics were able to gain richer insight into the overall outcomes that consumers receive. Where risks of poor outcomes were identified, some firms demonstrated appropriate actions taken to address the root cause, for instance, by updating customer support processes, or adjusting their operations.

## Overall findings – areas of improvement

### Aligning support processes to the target market [...] Some smaller firms carry out a simple annual review to check whether customers are getting the support they need. One firm used information it already collects (such as file checks, client feedback, complaints records and registers) to assess how well its support arrangements are working. The firm records any issues it identifies, sets out actions where improvements are needed, and summarises the key points for review and signoff by senior management.
